title: A resting book stays put because the table matches its weight
summary: On a level table, a book that is not speeding up is held by an upward push equal to its weight.
body: The third-law section of OpenStax Physics, Urone and Hinrichs, 26 March 2020, treats a resting object on a horizontal desk. If nothing is accelerating, the outside forces sum to zero, so the desk's upward push has the same size as the weight and the opposite direction. The page is careful: that match comes from the second law, and the desk's push is not the third-law partner of gravity. A slanted board is a different case, handled with ramps.

sources.title: 4.4 Newton's Third Law of Motion
sources.author: Paul Peter Urone and Roger Hinrichs
sources.note: Paraphrase only, not a quotation. OpenStax Physics, Paul Peter Urone and Roger Hinrichs, published 26 March 2020. The assigned licence for /books/physics/ is CC BY 4.0; the page footer also prints a noncommercial clause, so this card does not copy the sentence. Supports N = mg for a non-accelerating object on a horizontal surface, and the note that this is not a third-law pair.
